intro: The long residence route lets you apply for ILR after 10 years’ continuous lawful residence in the UK, across different visas. We check every gap and every absence before you apply on long residence.

rules.title: Absences
rules.text: Under the current rules you must not have spent more than 180 days outside the UK in any 12 months. Use our [absence calculator](/absence-calculator/).

rules.title: Gaps
rules.text: Some short gaps between visas can be disregarded if you applied in time. We check each one.

rules.title: Rules are changing
rules.text: The government’s settlement plans may change this route. [Read about the ILR changes](/ilr-changes-2026/)

boxTitle: Want a second pair of eyes before you apply?
boxText: A consultation costs far less than a refused application. We’ll check your case against the current rules and tell you honestly where you stand.

sections.heading: Long residence requirements
sections.text: You need 10 years’ continuous lawful residence in the UK, absences within the limits, the Life in the UK test, English at B1 level and good conduct. Time on most visas can count, which helps people who have moved between routes.

faqs.q: Does time as a student count towards long residence?
faqs.a: Yes, lawful time on a Student visa usually counts.

faqs.q: What if I had a gap between visas?
faqs.a: Some short gaps can be disregarded if you applied in time. We check your history.
